How one is built

Six images, then code puts every piece where it belongs

Grok paints an empty tank and each piece alone on magenta. compose_tank.py keys them out, sizes them to their slot, stands the two stands on the floor, hangs the corners and the lamp from the top edge, tints everything toward the tank's light and shadows what stands.

Every place the app draws a tank

Both key items whole on all eleven crops

Home on three phone sizes, the shop hero and grid tiles with their pan, the collection card, the Kin header, Focus, and the friend card. The window all of them keep is x 12–88 %, y 37–78 % of the plate.

Home band, 15 / 16 / 17 Pro / Max5 % off each side
Home band, iPhone SE9 % off the top
Shop hero tile37 % off the top
Shop grid tile, pannedup to 12 % off one side
Collection card22 % off top and bottom
Focus band, friend card11–13 % off top and bottom

Why not one painting. The first attempt asked Grok for the props inside the tank. Every model puts them against the frame edge, however the placement is worded, and the crops above then take half the chest on Home and leave slivers in the shop. Separate props fix it for good.

The fifteen

Two classics, eight the 18–24 crowd would pick, five for the gaps — all fifteen built

Each card is the tank's four colours, its two key items, and what will move once the art lands. The five outlined in gold came from the research: Ghibli is the top BetterCampus community theme, students asked the Canvas skin for Dark Academia, Lo-fi and Cottage, competition keeps the men, and the October cohort needs a seasonal drop. Prompts for all forty-five images are in design/tanks/GROK-TANK-PROMPTS.md.

What else can change

Six pieces a student keeps swapping, Finch-style

Finch's room is a bird and five fixed slots of furniture. Ours is the tank plus five slots: two stands every screen keeps, two corners, and a lamp at the top centre. Every piece is painted alone on magenta, so any piece fits any tank.

Stand L · Stand R

The two key items. Whole on every screen. Chest, diver, lamp, hoop, pumpkin, globe — one magenta image each, and because they are keyed and tinted, the Orbit rocket stands in Treasure sand just as happily. This is the collecting axis: 15 tanks × every stand you own.

Corner L · Corner R

Hanging from the top edge, top corners. Net, vine, string lights, neon sign, satellite, cobweb, icicles, pennants. Capped at 19% of the plate so they end above the name and coin chips instead of under them. Seen on Home and the Kin tab; the shop hero crops them. Decoration, not identity.

Light · the sixth piece

A lamp on a cord from the top centre. Brass lantern, paper lantern, neon ring, mirror ball, planet lamp. Its colour drives the tank's light rays, so a new lamp changes the whole mood of any tank. The fixture hangs from 8% down, clear of the Dynamic Island; code draws the stub of cord above it, which the island hides. The compositor measures every piece against the chips and the island and refuses one that is more than a cord's worth hidden.

Floor bits L · Floor bits R

Small things at the stands' feet. Coins and pearls, cassettes, cones, fallen leaves, mushrooms, a mug. Cheap to paint, big for personality. Sit in front of the stand; the bottom fade takes their lower edge.

Weather

Code-drawn, no art. Petals, snow, embers, coin glints, wisps, dust motes, rain streaks, fireflies. Already built as the drift layer; selling it is a switch. The one slot that can ship next week.

Companion · later

A small animated critter on the floor edges. Snail, jellyfish, crab, seahorse. Finch's micropets are the comparable. Each one needs a rig and a wander, so this is art plus code per critter.

Soundscape · later

One loop per tank. Rain for Lofi, waves for Reef, cafe hum, a lo-fi beat. The study-app angle no companion app has. Audio only, no art.

The floor rule, which slots cannot work without. Left: the first intricate tank put a coral cluster exactly where the chest stands, so the chest sat on rocks. Right: the same tank repainted under one rule — the floor is a bare, flat plane from the horizon down, and everything in the painting stands on the horizon line, hangs from the top, or hugs the far edge. Same horizon height on every tank, so every prop's feet land on the ground in every tank. compose_tank.py now refuses a tank whose stage is not bare, and the five shipping tanks fail that check: they need a repaint under the rule before they can take slots.

Not slots, on purpose: the discs, the ridges and the side dressing stay painted into the tank. They are what makes fifteen tanks read as one family.

All fifteen, built

Every theme painted, composed and checked

One run of build_sets.py: ninety images from the pack through Gemini, each tank checked against the rules and repainted once if it failed one, every set composed and passed. Sixteen minutes. The same script takes Grok's files when they arrive. Test art: some tanks came back as rooms with side walls, which the prompt now forbids, and Grok will paint the ones that ship.

Coffee, books, laptop, plant, trophy, radio, pennants, planes, string lights, calendar, desk lamp, moon lamp. Then the star, the ticked calendar, the hourglass, the open books, the diploma, the bell, the moon.

The shop

Fifteen themes, six pieces each, every piece fits every tank

Ninety images in the prompt pack. A theme's set is one tank plus five pieces. The shop's cards already show “your Home with one thing changed”, so a corner or a lamp is a card like any other. Mixing is the point: below, Treasure's room wearing Orbit's pieces and the Zen paper lantern, and Orbit wearing Treasure's set under the Vapor neon ring.

Tank (the painting)200–400 coins, as today

dropsA theme set a week after launch; Haunt's set only in October, Frost's in December. Plus never sells pieces — it sells faster refreshes and more picks, as the spec says.
startersLagoon ships with its two stands and lamp owned, so the first tap in the shop is a swap, not a purchase.
the lampThe cheapest way to make a tank feel new: one lamp recolours the light of every tank you own.

Prices are a suggestion; PLUS-SPEC.md stays the price table. The two demo sets are Gemini stand-ins; Orbit's rocky ridge is busier across the middle than the rule allows, which a Grok paint with a smooth middle fixes.

For students · not tied to a theme

Loose pieces to buy, earned pieces you cannot

Twelve theme-free pieces are what a student actually has on a desk: coffee cups, a book stack, a laptop, a plant, a trophy, a retro radio, pennants, paper planes, string lights, a calendar, a desk lamp, a moon lamp. They fill the shop between theme drops and are the first things a new student can afford. Seven more are earned, never sold, and sit greyed in the collection with the rule under them.

The five you ship · council verdict

Leave them alone until slots exist, then stand props on the originals

The clean-up edit looked like a fix and was not. Three reviewers on three models measured it: the model squashed each 3:2 painting 11% narrower instead of cropping it, the files came back half as sharp (Lagoon a 1.6× upscale), four of five lost mounds or plants, Deep grew a branch that was never there, and every one lost the stepping discs. A stage check passes on a plate that has lost its content. All three said the same thing on the second question: no slots on the old five at launch.

What the sheet shows. Left column ships today. Right column is the edit: the floor is bare, but Reef lost its coral fronds, Kelp its gold mounds and right-side kelp, Dusk every foreground mound. Props on top of these read as stickers on a blurry room.

The plan instead. Ship the five untouched. When slots are built, give each old tank its own slot boxes: every shipping plate has a bare strip wide enough for a prop inside the always-visible window (measured: nudge the left stand right by 0.10 on Lagoon and Reef, 0.06 on Kelp, 0.03 on Dusk; the right stand left by 0.07 on Reef and Dusk). Where a disc sits under the feet, the prop stands on it like a stepping stone. No art, no colour change to anyone's Home page. The floor rule stays mandatory for every NEW tank, and the clean-up script stays as a last resort, run at 2K with an eye check.

Not on the phone yet. The animation lives in the Sprout web build and type-checks. It goes into the app after you sign off the motion; the shop and collection stills never change.

Dark tanks need one Swift fix. The app never flips the status bar, so on Deep the clock is already dark on navy. Five more dark tanks make that a real bug.

Test art is Gemini, not Grok. The two live tanks prove the pipeline and the motion. The real ten get painted from the prompt pack.
